title: This Is Why I Meditate // Permission 2 Think

top_liked.author: @OceanusHelios
top_liked.text: I have never been a believer, but I habitually meditate.  It started when I was young and when I just needed to calm my thought and experience a bit of inner stillness and awareness of the outward world.

top_liked.author: @harmonychilden5326
top_liked.text: Another fantastic discussion. Meditation played a massive role in my deconversion from Christianity. Later I came to realize that the most profound benefit it gave was clarity of mind. It is why I could finally deeply explore and question my beliefs.

top_liked.author: @Chris-op7yt
top_liked.text: decades ago--we'll just call it a few years ago ok--i used to meditate, to help calm the mind. it did do that but also started having problems with dissociation and such, and stopped doing it. since i did some other upgrades to thinking etc and learning not to keep re-running…

top_liked.author: @alyssa_littlelightomine
top_liked.text:
Finally catching up on all the stuff I missed! I can't quite get the hang of meditation precisely, but I have a handful of things I do when I need to be more connected to myself
- angry feminist poetry for when I'm having feelings I can't identify and then I journal about…

top_liked.text:
I probably need to try some meditation when I wake up. I’ve also done yoga at time which is helpful.
